chunks: Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar al-Jaʿfarī asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man who has days due from the Month of Ramadan: may he make them up separately? He said:

“There is no harm in separating the make-up fasts of the Month of Ramadan. The only fasting that is not to be separated is the fast of the expiation for ẓihār, the expiation for blood, and the expiation for an oath.”

key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month in which the obligatory sawm is prescribed
key_terms.قَضَاءِ: making up an obligatory act missed earlier
key_terms.كَفَّارَةِ الدَّمِ: the expiation fast connected to bloodshed
key_terms.كَفَّارَةِ الظِّهَارِ: the expiation fast required for ẓihār
key_terms.كَفَّارَةِ الْيَمِينِ: the expiation fast related to a broken oath

ai.seo_question: Can missed fasts from Ramadan be made up on separate, non-consecutive days?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that missed fasts from Ramadan may be made up on non-consecutive days. It distinguishes Ramadan make-up fasts from certain expiatory fasts, which must be observed consecutively.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1998 - Sulaiman ibn Ja'far Al-Ja'fari asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha (as) about a man who has missed days from the Month of Ramadan. Can he make them up non-consecutively?

Imam (as) replied: "There is no harm in making up the fasts of the Month of Ramadan separately. The fasting that must not be separated is the fast of expiation for zhihar, expiation for shedding blood, and expiation for breaking an oath."
